vocabulary.example: I drink coffee in the morning.

grammar.explanation_en: Use 'like' to say you enjoy something, and 'don't like' to say you don't. Follow it directly with a noun: 'I like coffee', 'I don't like spicy food'. For polite offers, use 'Would you like ~?'.
grammar.explanation_ko: 무언가를 좋아하면 'like', 안 좋아하면 'don't like'를 씁니다. 뒤에 명사가 바로 옵니다: 'I like coffee'(저는 커피를 좋아해요), 'I don't like spicy food'(저는 매운 음식을 안 좋아해요). 정중하게 권할 때는 'Would you like ~?'를 씁니다.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.line: Are you hungry? Would you like some lunch?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.line: No, I don't. I like mild food.
dialogue.line_ko: 아니요, 안 좋아해요. 저는 순한 음식이 좋아요.

reading.title: My Favorite Meal
reading.text: I eat breakfast at seven every morning. I like rice and soup. I don't like coffee, so I drink tea instead. For dinner, I usually eat with my family. My mother's cooking is always delicious.
reading.text_ko: 저는 매일 아침 일곱 시에 아침을 먹어요. 저는 밥과 국을 좋아해요. 커피는 안 좋아해서 대신 차를 마셔요. 저녁에는 보통 가족과 함께 먹어요. 어머니의 요리는 항상 맛있어요.

explanation.en: The text says 'I eat breakfast at seven every morning.'
explanation.ko: 본문에 'I eat breakfast at seven every morning.'이라고 나옵니다.

explanation.en: The text says 'I drink tea instead.'
The text says 'I usually eat with my family.'
explanation.ko: 본문에 'I usually eat with my family.'라고 나옵니다.
